requirementSpec.intent: Build a polished Roblox main menu titled AURORA with Play, Settings, and Credits. Settings must open a panel containing a Music on/off toggle and Volume slider. Credits must open a small panel. Both panels must include Close controls. Support desktop and mobile. Use rich glossy cyan/cobalt artwork with thick navy edges, warm gold highlights, ornamental corner details, and a title plate. Use Gemini-generated matching skins and distinct icons while keeping text live and readable. Play must close the menu and fire a clearly named local hook for game integration. Include coherent hover and press animation, restrained native background layout decoration, and ensure panels open and close through the actual controller. Create only the requested features.

designPlan.artDirection: Premium Roblox fantasy-tech menu with a restrained native backdrop and a concentrated glossy centerpiece. The interface uses layered cyan and cobalt enamel surfaces wrapped by thick navy framing, then selectively lifted with warm gold rim highlights and small ornamental corner flourishes. A dedicated title plate crowns the stack so the live AURORA text feels ceremonial without baking text into art. The visual language should feel cohesive across button skins, panel skin, toggle pieces, slider track and handle, and the icon family, all planned as Gemini-generated matching artwork. Ornament stays structural and corner-bound so the center remains readable and the primary Play action stays dominant. Panels inherit the same skin kit at a slightly flatter depth so they clearly belong to the menu but do not outshine the root action stack. Text remains clean, bright, and largely unoutlined, relying on dark framed surfaces for contrast rather than heavy effects.

composition.focalPoint: A vertically stacked central menu composition with the title plate at top, a dominant Play button in the middle, and Settings/Credits grouped directly below as peer primary actions. Context panels emerge centered above the same composition so the screen never fragments.
secondaryRegions: title_header frames the live AURORA heading with a ceremonial plate.
settings_modal overlays the center with medium footprint and preserves visibility of the menu context beneath.
credits_modal overlays the center with a smaller footprint than settings.
background_frame supplies subtle anchored decoration only at edges and corners.
system_hooks holds nonvisual controller and play integration primitives.
composition.alignmentSystem: Strong centered vertical axis for title, primary CTA, and secondary action group. Primary actions align to the same width family as the menu stack. Modal internals use left-aligned labels with right-aligned control affordances for clear settings scanning, while close buttons pin to the top-right of each panel. Ornament aligns to panel and root corners, never floating independently.

visualSystem.colorRationale: Cyan drives interactivity and glossy energy, cobalt deepens body surfaces, and navy creates the thick framing requested. Gold is reserved for specular trims, title emphasis, and important rim accents so it reads premium instead of noisy. Background stays very dark and cool to let the menu stack glow forward. Secondary text softens into pale blue for hierarchy without introducing off-theme neutrals.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Thick navy outer framing with a slimmer inner cyan-gold highlight split. Buttons and panels use consistent rounded corners with heavier stroke weight on primary surfaces. Text is not globally outlined; only title plate and selected artwork carry baked edge richness.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Short, dense navy-black shadows for lift plus subtle cyan bloom near glossy edges. Main Play button gets the deepest shadow tier, peer main buttons one tier lower, and modals use broad soft drop shadows to separate from the root without excessive blur.

iconSystem.styleDescription: Gemini-generated icon family with front-facing fantasy-tech silhouettes inset into glossy medallion-ready button layouts. Shapes are clean and readable at small sizes, with cyan/cobalt bodies, navy edge definition, and selective gold accents for tips, hubs, or borders.

motionSystem.hover: Interactive controls softly lift and intensify their gloss band on mouse devices. The motion should feel premium and bounded, never floaty. Peer main buttons receive less amplitude than Play. Slider and toggle use focused affordance motion limited to handle/thumb glow and tiny lift.
motionSystem.press: All actionable controls compress slightly with a quick downward settle. Buttons scale subtly and darken their lower edge; toggle thumb compresses before switching; slider handle compresses on drag start.
motionSystem.entrance: Menu root fades and rises in together with the title plate leading by a fraction, then buttons cascade in quickly along the same vertical axis. Modals fade and scale from 0.96 to 1 with a short upward settle while dimming a light backdrop overlay.
motionSystem.release: Controls rebound to rest with a short eased return and reduced overshoot. Modal close reverses entrance with quick fade and slight scale down.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: Remove positional lift and scale offsets, keeping only quick opacity and color changes for hover/press and simple show/hide for modals.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch uses Activated and drag interactions only. No synthetic hover. Press feedback remains immediate and visible, especially on Play, Close, toggle, and slider handle.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds on touch because sounds were not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a sound system exists globally, do not bind menu-specific sounds; preserve silent operation rather than invent assets.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build _NexusDesktop with a centered ceremonial stack: title plate, dominant Play CTA, then two peer main action buttons for Settings and Credits. Settings modal appears medium-sized with two neat horizontal rows; credits modal stays notably smaller. Decorative corner details remain visible on frame and panels because there is room for them.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Build _NexusMobile independently rather than scaling desktop. Keep the same semantic nodeNames under the mobile tree. Use a taller stacked root frame with reduced ornament density, broader buttons, and larger touch targets. Settings modal becomes wider and more vertical; the volume control may place its label above the slider if needed for clean touch interaction. Credits stays compact but uses wider wrapped text. Primary hierarchy remains Play first and largest, with Settings and Credits preserved as peer main actions.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Use the mobile canonical group when min viewport dimension is below 600, otherwise tablet can retain the desktop composition with slightly expanded padding and modal widths between phone and desktop. Ornament detail can be restored one step above phone density while preserving touch-safe control sizes.

implementationNotes: View.build() must create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile root Frame groups up front, each containing the same semantic nodeName descendants for builder verification.
Desktop group visible initially; runtime selects the mobile group when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) < 600.
Use local View helper functions for repeated construction: createPanelSurface, createGlossButton, createCornerOrnaments, createSettingsRow, createBackground, createTitleText.
Use a shared ButtonEffects module for hover/press behavior on Play, Settings, Credits, and both Close buttons; do not duplicate per-button tween logic.
Keep all labels and the AURORA title as live TextLabel/TextButton text; title plate and button skins remain artwork only.
For volume slider, split stable visual pieces under VolumeSlider such as VolumeSliderTrack, VolumeSliderFill, and VolumeSliderHandle while keeping adjust_volume bound to the parent control.
For music toggle, split stable visual pieces such as MusicToggleOff, MusicToggleOn, and MusicToggleThumb while keeping toggle_music bound to the parent control.

Panel controller must actually open and close SettingsPanel and CreditsPanel in the controller, not just style hidden mocks. Ensure only one panel is visible at a time unless intentionally changed later.
Play action must close the menu root and then invoke a clearly named local hook function represented by PlayIntegrationHook, such as firePlayRequestedHook, for game-side integration.

Use generated artwork strategy consistently for the full requested skin kit and icon family: play, settings, credits, close, panel skin, button skins, slider track, slider handle, toggle on/off pieces, title plate, and corner ornaments.
No audio assets should be fabricated. Leave interface silent because sounds were not requested.
Use UIAspectRatioConstraint on title plate and ornamental image pieces so decorative artwork preserves intended proportions during resize.
Use UITextSizeConstraint on all live text-bearing components to preserve readability across desktop, phone portrait, and tablet.
Apply a dim overlay within modal CanvasGroup during panel open states if needed for focus, but keep it subtle and do not obscure the menu art excessively.
Do not add extra destinations, currencies, progression, or invented credits systems; credits content remains a simple live text block inside the small panel.

iconSystem.styleDescription: Gemini-generated icon family with front-facing fantasy-tech silhouettes inset into glossy medallion-ready button layouts. Shapes are clean and readable at small sizes, with cyan/cobalt bodies, navy edge definition, and selective gold accents for tips, hubs, or borders.

motionSystem.hover: Interactive controls softly lift and intensify their gloss band on mouse devices. The motion should feel premium and bounded, never floaty. Peer main buttons receive less amplitude than Play. Slider and toggle use focused affordance motion limited to handle/thumb glow and tiny lift.
motionSystem.press: All actionable controls compress slightly with a quick downward settle. Buttons scale subtly and darken their lower edge; toggle thumb compresses before switching; slider handle compresses on drag start.
motionSystem.entrance: Menu root fades and rises in together with the title plate leading by a fraction, then buttons cascade in quickly along the same vertical axis. Modals fade and scale from 0.96 to 1 with a short upward settle while dimming a light backdrop overlay.
motionSystem.release: Controls rebound to rest with a short eased return and reduced overshoot. Modal close reverses entrance with quick fade and slight scale down.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: Remove positional lift and scale offsets, keeping only quick opacity and color changes for hover/press and simple show/hide for modals.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch uses Activated and drag interactions only. No synthetic hover. Press feedback remains immediate and visible, especially on Play, Close, toggle, and slider handle.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds on touch because sounds were not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a sound system exists globally, do not bind menu-specific sounds; preserve silent operation rather than invent assets.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build _NexusDesktop with a centered ceremonial stack: title plate, dominant Play CTA, then two peer main action buttons for Settings and Credits. Settings modal appears medium-sized with two neat horizontal rows; credits modal stays notably smaller. Decorative corner details remain visible on frame and panels because there is room for them.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Build _NexusMobile independently rather than scaling desktop. Keep the same semantic nodeNames under the mobile tree. Use a taller stacked root frame with reduced ornament density, broader buttons, and larger touch targets. Settings modal becomes wider and more vertical; the volume control may place its label above the slider if needed for clean touch interaction. Credits stays compact but uses wider wrapped text. Primary hierarchy remains Play first and largest, with Settings and Credits preserved as peer main actions.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Use the mobile canonical group when min viewport dimension is below 600, otherwise tablet can retain the desktop composition with slightly expanded padding and modal widths between phone and desktop. Ornament detail can be restored one step above phone density while preserving touch-safe control sizes.

implementationNotes: View.build() must create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile root Frame groups up front, each containing the same semantic nodeName descendants for builder verification.
Desktop group visible initially; runtime selects the mobile group when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) < 600.
Use local View helper functions for repeated construction: createPanelSurface, createGlossButton, createCornerOrnaments, createSettingsRow, createBackground, createTitleText.
Use a shared ButtonEffects module for hover/press behavior on Play, Settings, Credits, and both Close buttons; do not duplicate per-button tween logic.
Keep all labels and the AURORA title as live TextLabel/TextButton text; title plate and button skins remain artwork only.
For volume slider, split stable visual pieces under VolumeSlider such as VolumeSliderTrack, VolumeSliderFill, and VolumeSliderHandle while keeping adjust_volume bound to the parent control.
For music toggle, split stable visual pieces such as MusicToggleOff, MusicToggleOn, and MusicToggleThumb while keeping toggle_music bound to the parent control.

Panel controller must actually open and close SettingsPanel and CreditsPanel in the controller, not just style hidden mocks. Ensure only one panel is visible at a time unless intentionally changed later.
Play action must close the menu root and then invoke a clearly named local hook function represented by PlayIntegrationHook, such as firePlayRequestedHook, for game-side integration.

Use generated artwork strategy consistently for the full requested skin kit and icon family: play, settings, credits, close, panel skin, button skins, slider track, slider handle, toggle on/off pieces, title plate, and corner ornaments.
No audio assets should be fabricated. Leave interface silent because sounds were not requested.
Use UIAspectRatioConstraint on title plate and ornamental image pieces so decorative artwork preserves intended proportions during resize.
Use UITextSizeConstraint on all live text-bearing components to preserve readability across desktop, phone portrait, and tablet.
Apply a dim overlay within modal CanvasGroup during panel open states if needed for focus, but keep it subtle and do not obscure the menu art excessively.
Do not add extra destinations, currencies, progression, or invented credits systems; credits content remains a simple live text block inside the small panel.

changeInstructions: Create a new main menu for AURORA.
Implement Play, Settings, and Credits as the only main actions.
Implement Settings panel with Music on/off toggle and Volume slider.
Implement Credits as a small panel.
Add Close controls to both panels.
Make Play close the menu and fire a clearly named local hook for game integration.
Support desktop and mobile layouts.
Use Gemini-generated matching skins and icons.
Keep text live and readable.
Ensure panel open/close behavior is handled by the actual controller.
Use coherent hover and press animation.
Keep background layout native with restrained decoration.
